title: Implementation Plan
description: Phased implementation plan with tasks, dependencies, and test expectations at three levels. Designed for zero-context handoff: a coder receives a task and can implement without design doc access; an auditor receives a task and can verify without plan-level context.

schema_version.description: MODEL-REVISION-ADDITION format. Bump MODEL for breaking changes, REVISION for backward-compatible structural changes, ADDITION for new optional fields.

feature.description: Feature identifier, matches design doc and context packet naming

design_doc.description: Path to the design document this plan implements

grounding.description: How the design doc was grounded to the codebase. Persists the full concept map so staleness detection can diff against fresh context packets without repeating Step 1.

context_packets.description: Context packet filenames used for grounding. Used for staleness detection — when packets refresh, diff files_analyzed lists against concept_map.

concept_map.description: Design doc concepts mapped to codebase constructs. Every design doc concept must appear here as grounded or with a resolution. This is the bridge between design intent and implementation reality.

approach_rationale.description: Why this approach was chosen, with evidence references. For single-approach features, state why the approach was obvious (e.g., 'follows existing scorer pattern in producer/scoring.py').

alternatives_considered.description: Other approaches evaluated during Step 3 divergent exploration. Empty array if Step 3 was skipped (single clear approach).

phases.description: Ordered list of implementation phases. Array index implies execution order. Dependencies between phases form a DAG — no circular dependencies.

design_tests.description: Design-level integration tests spanning all phases. Cover the design doc's acceptance criteria end-to-end. Runnable only after all phases complete.

gate_script.description: Comprehensive quality gate script that runs all checks

design_concept.description: Concept as referenced in the design doc (e.g., 'scoring weights', 'pipeline stage registration')

codebase_construct.description: The mapped construct with location (e.g., 'ScoringWeights in producer/config.py:23'). Use '???' if unresolved.

source.description: Which context packet or exploration provided this mapping (e.g., '_codebase.json types', 'explorer response 2025-02-28')

status.description: grounded=confirmed in context, resolved=was a gap but info_request answered it, gap_blocking=unresolved and blocks planning, gap_non_blocking=can resolve during task detailing

resolution.description: How a gap was resolved (e.g., 'Explorer confirmed RegistrationAPI uses decorator pattern in pipeline/registry.py:45'). Required when status is 'resolved'.

name.description: Short name for the approach (e.g., 'Polling-based sync')

summary.description: What this approach would have looked like

rejected_reason.description: Why this approach was not chosen, with evidence

name.description: Short descriptive name for the phase

capability.description: What capability this phase delivers (one sentence, concrete). Must be a verifiable behavior, not a code change description.

verification.description: How to prove the phase is complete. Must be demonstrable without requiring future phases.

dependencies.description: Phase IDs that must complete before this phase

rationale.description: Why this phase boundary exists (not a different one)

design_doc_sections.description: Which design doc sections this phase implements (e.g., '3.2 Batch Selection', '4.1 Constraint Handling'). Enables auditor traceability — every design doc requirement must map to at least one phase.

phase_tests.description: Phase-level integration tests verifying the capability works end-to-end within phase scope. Runnable at phase completion with no dependency on future phases.

phase_context.description: One-line summary of the phase this task belongs to, so a context-free coder understands the larger goal. Format: 'Phase N: {capability}' (e.g., 'Phase 2: Batch selection with constraints').

target_files.description: Files the coder will create or modify (e.g., 'producer/ops_batch.py'). Enables orchestrator conflict detection for parallel tasks.

reference_files.description: Files the coder should read but not modify (e.g., 'consumer/scoring.py:45-67'). Include line ranges when pointing to specific patterns.

requirements.description: Exact behaviors the implementation must satisfy. Each requirement should be testable. Use exact types, function signatures, file paths.

limitations.description: What the task must NOT do. Explicit scope boundaries prevent coder drift.

considerations.description: Non-obvious factors: edge cases, existing patterns to follow, performance concerns, thread safety.

suggestions.description: Recommended approaches, relevant code references (not mandates — coder may deviate with justification)

dependencies.description: Task IDs that must complete first

review_level.description: 1=no auditor, 2=phase-end audit, 3=full task auditor. Based on risk, not convenience.

review_focus.description: What the auditor should specifically verify beyond standard requirements check. Present on review_level 2-3 tasks. Tells the auditor WHERE to look — the strategist's specific concerns (e.g., 'Verify floating-point precision in weighted sum', 'Confirm no regression in existing score_roi consumers').

queries.description: Questions the coder must resolve before implementing. Forces uncertainty declaration — prevents strategist from guessing and coder from assuming.

test_expectations.description: What tests must verify for this task. Each expectation maps to at least one test the coder writes during TDD.

session_log.description: Path to session log for this task (populated during execution)

id.description: Unique test expectation identifier (phase-task-expectation format, e.g., 'te-01-01-01'). Enables auditor to programmatically verify coverage against implemented tests.

description.description: What this test verifies in plain language (e.g., 'Zero-weight fields excluded from computation')

requirement_refs.description: Which requirements this expectation verifies (by index or keyword). Ensures every requirement has at least one test expectation covering it.

acceptance_criteria.description: Link to design doc criteria (e.g., 'Design Doc Section 4.2 Acceptance Criteria')
